aiReview.summary: Official Google AI for Developers hub covering Gemini API docs, API reference, pricing, AI Studio, Gemma, and related tools. High-relevance canonical entry for a Gemini directory.
evidence: Excerpt title and URL are Gemini Developer API / Google AI for Developers at https://ai.google.dev/
Nav lists Gemini docs (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs), API reference (ai.google.dev/api), and pricing.
Solutions include Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Gemma, Google AI Edge, and Responsible GenAI Toolkit.
Candidate source is official-web with empty riskFlags and confidenceScore 1.
uncertainty: Current free-tier limits and exact commercial terms are not fully specified in the excerpt.
Homepage excerpt is truncated and does not include full API method coverage.
aiReview.tagline: Official docs, APIs, and tools for Google models
aiReview.description: Find API docs, pricing, studio access, open-model guides, on-device options, and responsible-AI resources in one developer hub.
pros: Canonical ai.google.dev site with Gemini API docs, API reference, and pricing links.
Also indexes AI Studio, Gemma docs, on-device/edge paths, and responsible-AI guidance.
Maintained official property with multilingual navigation and community forum links.
cons: Homepage is a navigation hub rather than a self-contained tutorial or SDK.
API usage still depends on keys, quotas, and paid tiers documented on the pricing page.

Security review of src/ was not performed beyond README claims.
Issue quality and whether the four open issues are blocking.
aiReview.tagline: Minimal JS wrapper for Gemini ask, chat, and files
aiReview.description: Call Gemini from ES modules with short ask/chat APIs, streaming, embeddings, and automatic file uploads.

Repository is not archived and has modest community traction (115 stars, 19 forks).
cons: Last push is 2024-06-24, so models and API surface may be outdated versus Google’s current SDK.
GPL-3.0 can constrain reuse compared with official Apache-licensed clients.
It is a third-party simplification, not an official Google library.

aiReview.summary: Community MIT Ruby client for Gemini via Generative Language API, AI Studio, and Vertex AI, with streaming, embeddings, tools, and safety settings. Last GitHub push was July 2025, so verify model names against current Google APIs before production use.
evidence: Repo description and README: Ruby gem for Vertex AI, Generative Language API, or AI Studio.
Facts: MIT, not archived, 190 stars, 32 forks, topics include gemini and google-vertex-ai.
pushed_at 2025-07-09; gem version 4.3.0 in README install instructions.
README covers stream_generate_content, embeddings, tools, JSON, safety, and multiple credential modes.
uncertainty: Whether 4.3.0 tracks Gemini 2.x / latest REST fields without unlisted gaps.
Current RubyGems download volume and issue resolution rate.
Runtime security of credential file handling was not audited beyond README.
aiReview.tagline: Low-level Ruby client for Vertex and AI Studio APIs
aiReview.description: Call Gemini from Ruby with API keys or Vertex credentials, including streaming, embeddings, JSON mode, and function calling.
pros: Supports Generative Language API keys, Vertex service accounts, ADC, and a global Vertex endpoint.
README documents generate/stream, embeddings, system instructions, token counting, JSON schema, tools, and safety settings.
MIT-licensed Ruby gem with specs and a published gemspec (gemini-ai ~> 4.3.0).
Includes credential and IAM security disclaimers rather than hiding GCP access risks.
cons: Not an official Google SDK; community maintenance (190 stars, last push 2025-07-09).
Quick-start examples still default to gemini-pro, which may lag current model IDs.
19 open issues on GitHub at review time.

uncertainty: Whether the code still works against current Gemini API versions and auth.

aiReview.tagline: Self-host Gemini chat and vision in Telegram
aiReview.description: Deploy a Telegram bot that routes text to Gemini Pro and images to Pro Vision, with context and Docker or shell setup.

cons: Last GitHub push is dated 2024-10-18; Gemini Pro/Pro Vision naming is outdated.

aiReview.summary: Deprecated browser-only Gemini chat UI (MIT) that stores the API key locally and talks to Google. Useful as a historical example, not as a maintained developer resource.
evidence: GitHub README title is Deprecated and states the project will no longer be maintained.
Repo metadata: TypeScript, MIT, ~69 stars, chat pages under src/pages/Chat.
README: API key stored in browser; optional proxy from Setup; docker compose up.
uncertainty: Whether the Vercel demo still works and which Gemini model/API version it calls.
Current security of key handling and the optional proxy path in source.
aiReview.tagline: Deprecated local chat frontend for Gemini API keys
aiReview.description: Run a Vite/TypeScript chat UI that keeps your Gemini API key in the browser and sends requests to Google, including optional Docker.
pros: README describes a pure front-end chat app that stores the API key in the browser and calls Google servers.
Includes Docker Compose, a Dockerfile, and notes for Vercel deploy.
MIT-licensed TypeScript/Vite project with a public changelog of chat-history and proxy features.
cons: The repository is explicitly marked deprecated and no longer maintained.
Client-side API key storage and optional request proxy increase exposure if the demo is hosted.
Docs are thin (npm start, screenshots) and the GitHub listing is renamed away from the original URL.

uncertainty: Full article body could not be fetched (HTTP 403).
Cannot verify code samples, model names, or whether screenshots/APIs are still accurate.

aiReview.tagline: Use Cloud Code templates to try the Gemini API
aiReview.description: Walks through testing the Gemini API with Google Cloud Code application templates for a first GCP-based experiment.
pros: Published on Google Cloud Community by Romin Irani and targets Gemini API usage.
Focuses on Cloud Code application templates as a concrete getting-started path.
Article is a short (~5 minute) tutorial format suitable for a directory of learning links.
cons: Content is from December 2023 and may not match current Gemini API or Cloud Code flows.

Not an official SDK, CLI, or continuously maintained code repository.

aiReview.summary: Paid Udemy course (~4h) covering Gemini concepts, prompting, Vertex AI Studio, and Gemini API in Python; curriculum still references Bard and Gemini Pro Vision and shows last updated June 2024 despite an October 2025 marketing line, so treat it as a dated paid tutorial rather than a primary developer resource.
evidence: Udemy title and description: Google Gemini AI Masterclass; UPDATED October 2025 - From Basic to Advanced Generative Artificial Intelligence on Google Gemini.
Course stats: 4.1/5 from 137 ratings, 539 students, 7 sections, 33 lectures, 3h 50m.
Last updated 6/2024; instructor Renaldi Gondosubroto.
Learning outcomes mention Gemini API, Gemini Pro, Google Cloud, Vertex AI Studio, and a lecture Using Google Bard with Gemini.
Objectives mention prompt engineering and deploying generative AI with Google Cloud.
uncertainty: Cannot verify lecture accuracy, SDK versions, or whether API code still runs.
Cannot confirm current price or refund policy without checkout.
Image-generation claims vs Gemini Pro Vision may not match current model lineup.
aiReview.tagline: Paid course on Gemini prompting, Vertex, and API basics
aiReview.description: Teaches Gemini fundamentals, prompt engineering, Vertex AI Studio, and Python API use for text, code, and vision in a short paid video course.
pros: Curriculum includes Gemini API text generation, parameters, code generation, and Vertex AI Studio playground.
Includes a lecture on caution and responsible use of LLMs.
Public page lists ratings, student count, and a structured 7-section outline.
cons: Udemy page says last updated 6/2024 while marketing copy claims October 2025.
Content still covers Google Bard, which is outdated naming and product context.
Paid third-party video course, not official Google docs or maintained open-source samples.

Weak fit for a Gemini developer directory because it is a commercial class, mixes vendors, and still teaches Google Bard-era workflows rather than current Gemini API implementation.
evidence: canonicalUrl is udemy.com/course/testing-quality-engineering-gen-ai-examples-gpt-bard
og:title is Accelerated Software Engineering Chat GPT and AI Agents
Learning objectives include Main Features of Google GEMINI AI and Connect to CHAT GPT API plus Bard-named test-framework labs
Meta: 4.4/5 from 3218 ratings, 10602 students, last updated 9/2025
uncertainty: Cannot verify lecture quality or whether Gemini API code is current versus Bard chat UI

aiReview.tagline: Paid course on ChatGPT and Gemini for QA engineers

pros: Course page lists Gemini feature coverage plus ChatGPT API connection and testing/CI examples.

cons: URL slug and several objectives still say Google Bard, so Gemini API currency is unclear.

What you'll learn bullets focus on Bing Chat, Image Creator, Microsoft Edge, Google Bard, and ChatGPT conversations.
URL slug still includes google-bard; no API, SDK, or code labs described.
uncertainty: Full paid lecture quality and whether Gemini API is covered beyond chat UI.

aiReview.tagline: Beginner prompting course for consumer AI chat apps
aiReview.description: Teaches ChatGPT, Gemini/Bard, and Bing Chat prompting, image tools, and Edge features for everyday productivity, not API development.
pros: Course page lists 53 lectures totaling about 2h 13m and was last updated August 2025.

cons: Content targets end-user chatbot and Edge productivity, not the Gemini API, SDKs, or production integration.

It is a paid Udemy course; lecture quality cannot be verified from the public syllabus alone.

aiReview.tagline: Paid Python course on Gemini APIs, AI Studio, and Streamlit
aiReview.description: Teaches Gemini API and Python SDK usage, AI Studio prompts, multimodal inputs, generation parameters, chat agents, and Streamlit UIs.

Fit versus official API docs for an implementation-focused directory.
aiReview.tagline: Official technical report on a multimodal model family
aiReview.description: Read the 2023 technical report on Ultra, Pro, and Nano multimodal models, benchmarks, and deployment via AI Studio and Vertex AI.

cons: Does not document Gemini API usage, SDKs, or implementation samples.

aiReview.summary: 2023 arXiv survey of generative AI research trends (MoE, multimodality, AGI speculation), not a Gemini API implementation guide. Weak fit for a developer-resource directory.
evidence: arXiv:2312.10868 abstract describes a survey of generative AI, Gemini, speculated Q*, MoE, multimodality, and preprint/peer-review issues.
Candidate type is web_url to a PDF, not code, CLI, or official Google AI docs.
No facts.readme with APIs or samples; source is a curated awesome-list link only.
uncertainty: Peer-review status versus later journal version not fully verified in this pass.
Citation quality and factual accuracy of the survey body were not audited line-by-line.
aiReview.tagline: Survey of generative AI research trends and ethics
aiReview.description: Reviews generative AI landscape, multimodal models, MoE, and academic preprint challenges; no SDK or API how-to.
pros: Public arXiv preprint with a stated abstract covering Gemini-era generative AI research themes.
Discusses multimodal learning, Mixture of Experts, ethics, and scholarly-communication issues.
Licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 on arXiv.
cons: Does not document the Gemini API, SDKs, or implementation patterns.
Dated December 2023 preprint; includes speculative Q* discussion rather than current product docs.
Better suited as background reading than as a maintained developer resource.

aiReview.summary: Third-party 2023 arXiv evaluation of Gemini Pro vs GPT-3.5 Turbo on language tasks, with public code. Useful background reading, not a Gemini API or SDK implementation resource.
evidence: Abstract states Gemini Pro was close but slightly inferior to GPT-3.5 Turbo on all benchmarked tasks.
Authors list failure modes including multi-digit math, multiple-choice order sensitivity, and aggressive content filtering.
Listed in Awesome-Google-Gemini-AI README as a research link, not a tool.
uncertainty: Current maintenance of the github.com/neulab/gemini-benchmark repo was not verified in this pass.
Peer-review or journal status beyond arXiv is not confirmed here.
aiReview.tagline: Third-party language-task eval vs GPT-3.5 Turbo
aiReview.description: Compares language, math, code, translation, and agent tasks with reproducible code and notes failure modes such as digit math and filters.
pros: arXiv paper (2312.11444) from NeuLab authors with a stated third-party comparison of Gemini Pro and GPT-3.5 Turbo.
Covers 10 datasets spanning reasoning, knowledge QA, math, translation, code generation, and instruction-following agents.
Points to public reproduction code and data at github.com/neulab/gemini-benchmark.
cons: It is a 2023 snapshot of Gemini Pro, not current Gemini API documentation or client libraries.
Does not teach how to call Google AI Studio or production Gemini endpoints.
Findings may not transfer to later Gemini model versions.

evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.17661 — Wang & Zhao, 2023-12-29, cs.CL/cs.AI/cs.CV.
Abstract describes evaluation of Gemini vs GPT-4V and other models on commonsense tasks, not API usage.
Listed in Awesome-Google-Gemini-AI README as a paper title/link only.
uncertainty: Citation count, venue acceptance, and whether code/data were released were not verified.
Which Gemini API surface (if any) was used is not specified in the abstract.
aiReview.tagline: Academic eval of MLLM commonsense reasoning
aiReview.description: Evaluates multimodal LLMs on 12 commonsense reasoning datasets and reports competitive results plus remaining failure modes.
pros: Peer-style preprint with a stated method: 12 commonsense datasets (11 language-only, one multimodal) across several LLMs/MLLMs.
Directly discusses Gemini’s commonsense reasoning versus other models, including limits of HellaSWAG-only claims.
Hosted on arXiv with a clear abstract, authors, and subject categories.
cons: Not developer documentation, SDK, or sample code for the Gemini API.
Snapshot from late 2023; model versions and benchmarks may be outdated.
No maintenance, tutorials, or production integration guidance.

evidence: PubMed abstract title and journal match the candidate URL.

Candidate was discovered only as a README link in an awesome list, not as official Gemini docs.
uncertainty: Full article body beyond the abstract was not evaluated for hidden code or API notes.
Paywall or journal access details for non-PMC readers were not verified.
aiReview.tagline: Academic Gemini vs ChatGPT comparison in eye care
aiReview.description: Peer-reviewed paper compares Gemini and ChatGPT in ophthalmology; no API or SDK guidance for builders.
pros: Indexed PubMed article (PMID 38355668) in Eye (Lond) 2024 with DOI 10.1038/s41433-024-02958-w.
PMC full text is available (PMC11126415).
Authors declare no competing interests.
cons: Does not document Gemini API usage, SDKs, or sample code.
Clinical comparison paper, not a developer tutorial or tool.
MeSH terms emphasize ophthalmology and AI, not Google AI Studio or client libraries.

aiReview.summary: Official Google YouTube demo (Dec 2023) showing Gemini multimodal reasoning; useful as product context, not as API docs or implementation guidance. Latency and outputs were shortened for the demo.
evidence: Video title and channel: The capabilities of multimodal AI | Gemini Demo, Google, 6:22, ~3.3M views.
Description states natively multimodal Gemini and that latency was reduced and outputs shortened.
Listed in Awesome-Google-Gemini-AI README as a YouTube demo link, not a code resource.
uncertainty: Whether the 2023 demo still matches current Gemini API behavior.
Exact relationship between demo UI and public Gemini API/AI Studio surfaces.
aiReview.tagline: Official multimodal Gemini capability demo video
aiReview.description: Watch Google’s 2023 Gemini demo of reasoning over text, images, audio, video, and code, with a note that latency was reduced.
pros: Published on the official Google YouTube channel on 2023-12-06.
Shows multimodal interaction across text, images, audio, video, and code.
Description links to DeepMind Gemini pages and notes demo latency/output shortening.
cons: No SDK, API samples, or implementation steps for developers.
Content is a staged demo, so it is not a current or complete capability reference.
Does not document production constraints, quotas, or safety APIs.

aiReview.summary: Official Google consumer promo of Bard/Gemini Pro scripting a Mark Rober-style video; it is not a developer API, SDK, or implementation guide and is a weak fit for a Gemini developer directory.
evidence: canonicalUrl is youtube.com/watch?v=mHZSrtl4zX0 titled “AI makes a Mark Rober video | Bard with Gemini Pro”.
Search results list it as a Google-channel video (~6:19, tens of millions of views).
Candidate type is web_url with no README, code, or API facts.
uncertainty: Exact upload date, current view count, and full transcript were not fetched.
Whether the video mentions any developer console or API endpoints is unverified.
aiReview.tagline: Google promo of Gemini Pro scripting a science video
aiReview.description: Watch Google show Bard with Gemini Pro drafting a Mark Rober-style YouTube video. Consumer demo, not API docs or sample code.
pros: Hosted on Google’s official YouTube channel as a product demonstration.
Title and listing explicitly mention Bard with Gemini Pro.
Public, high-visibility video with no malware or exploit content.
cons: Does not teach Gemini API usage, SDKs, or production integration.
Bard branding is outdated relative to current Gemini developer surfaces.
Consumer marketing demo rather than a maintainable developer resource.

aiReview.summary: Short 2023 Android walkthrough of Gemini Pro/Vision in a sample furniture-suggestion app; useful for beginners but API surfaces (MakerSuite, model names, Studio wizard) are dated.
evidence: YouTube video i7PJwg0lrU0, channel Philipp Lackner, uploaded 2023-12-27, duration 8:13, ~131K views.
Transcript covers makersuite.google.com API keys, Gemini Pro vs Vision, Android Studio Gemini starter, and model.generateContent with bitmap plus prompt.
Listed in Awesome-Google-Gemini-AI README as a YouTube tutorial, not official Google docs.
uncertainty: Whether linked sample code still compiles against current Gemini Android SDKs.
Whether the video remains the best Android Gemini intro versus newer official tutorials.
aiReview.tagline: Android walkthrough of Gemini image-and-text generation
aiReview.description: Watch an Android sample that sends a room photo plus a prompt to Gemini and reads the text response, including generative model setup.
pros: Shows Gemini generative-model setup and generateContent with image plus text on Android.
Demonstrates a concrete multimodal sample (room photo to furniture suggestions).
Creator is an established Android educator; the video is about eight minutes with a full walkthrough.
cons: Published December 2023, so MakerSuite, Gemini Pro/Vision names, and the Iguana project wizard are outdated.
Does not cover current Google AI Studio, SDK versions, or production key handling.
Description mainly promotes paid Android mentoring and courses rather than a maintained sample repo.

cons: Marketing overview with little code, SDK guidance, or API reference on the page itself.
Canonical URL redirected to /ai/gemini and mixes preview products with GA offerings.

Links to set-up, data governance, release notes, and Google Cloud compliance.
Creative Commons documentation license; Apache 2.0 for code samples on the site.

Whether this listing matches a Gemini API-focused awesome list versus Google Cloud Gemini products.
aiReview.tagline: AI chat, completion, and error help in GCP notebooks
aiReview.description: Official docs covering notebook chat, code completion and generation, cell explanations, and error fixes in Colab Enterprise on Google Cloud.
pros: Official Google Cloud documentation last updated 2026-10-07 with linked setup, chat, completion, and error-help pages.
Describes concrete notebook features: chat, inline completion, generate-from-description, explain cells, and syntax-error fixes.
Points to Gemini for Google Cloud data-governance and compliance documentation.
cons: Targets Colab Enterprise on Google Cloud rather than the Gemini Developer API or SDKs.
Overview page has no runnable samples; implementation detail lives on child pages.
Requires Google Cloud / Colab Enterprise setup rather than a free standalone API tutorial.

Meta description: Learn about responsible AI in Google Cloud.
uncertainty: How often this page is the primary entry versus related Vertex/Gemini API safety docs.
Whether the awesome-list audience expects Developer API resources more than Cloud Code Assist policy pages.
aiReview.tagline: Cloud AI safety limits, risks, and content filters
aiReview.description: Explains LLM risks, Cloud Gemini product limits, and safety filtering so teams can evaluate and use generative assistance more carefully.
pros: Official Google Cloud docs last updated 2026-10-07 with a clear structure on capabilities, limitations, and filtering.

Points to Google AI principles, the Acceptable Use Policy, and related prompt/citation docs.
cons: Targets Gemini for Google Cloud products, not the consumer Gemini Developer API or SDKs.
Does not include code samples or API integration steps.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Skills intermediate course covering Gemini prompting, Python SDK function calling, and deploying a Streamlit app on Cloud Run. Short, vendor-maintained training with a skill badge and challenge lab; not a standalone SDK or production library.
evidence: Canonical page https://www.skills.google/paths/236/course_templates/978 titled Develop Gen AI Apps with Gemini and Streamlit.
Meta description: text generation, function calls with Python SDK and Gemini API, Streamlit on Cloud Run, Gemini prompting, Cloud Shell, Docker.
Page labels: 45 minutes, Intermediate, Updated about 2 months ago; GEAR program link.
Discovered from rominirani/awesome-gemini-for-google-cloud curated README.
uncertainty: Whether labs are free with credits or require a paid Google Skills subscription.
Exact lab modules, model versions, and code quality cannot be verified without enrolling.
Redirect from cloudskillsboost.google to skills.google; long-term URL stability.
aiReview.tagline: Hands-on labs for Gemini apps with Streamlit and Cloud Run
aiReview.description: Learn Gemini prompting, Python SDK function calls, and deploy Streamlit apps as Cloud Run containers in an intermediate skill-badge course.
pros: Hosted on Google Skills as an official intermediate skill-badge course last updated about two months ago.
Curriculum explicitly includes Gemini API text generation, function calling with the Python SDK, and Streamlit plus Cloud Run deployment.
Offers a challenge lab path to earn the badge without completing every module.
cons: Listed duration is about 45 minutes, so depth is limited compared with full documentation or sample repos.
Hands-on labs typically require a Google Skills/Qwiklabs account and may consume credits not visible on the public page.

Page title and heading report thousands of results for "gemini"
Listed items include consumer courses such as productivity with Google Gemini and Gemini Gems
meta robots includes noindex; meta description is generic LinkedIn Learning marketing copy
Discovered only as a README link labeled Gemini courses on LinkedIn Learning
uncertainty: Which specific courses remain available without a LinkedIn Learning login
How much content covers Gemini API versus Gemini consumer products
Course quality and maintenance of individual catalog items
aiReview.tagline: Paywalled search of Google Gemini video courses
aiReview.description: Opens a paid course search for Google Gemini assistants, prompting, and workplace use rather than a fixed API tutorial.
pros: The search currently returns many Google Gemini–related courses and clips.
Several listed courses cover prompting, Gemini apps, and related Google AI product use.
The page is a known commercial training catalog rather than an unknown third-party site.
cons: The URL is a keyword search with thousands of mixed results, not a curated course list.
Content is subscription-gated and not a first-party Gemini API implementation guide.
Results mix consumer Gemini, Notebook, Gems, and unrelated hits, so API relevance is weak.
The page is marked noindex and result order can change over time.

https://www.udacity.com/enrollment/cd13416 redirects to Udacity auth sign-in.
Listed in rominirani/awesome-gemini-for-google-cloud README as Gemini API by Google - Udacity.
uncertainty: Actual lesson content, code samples, and whether they match current Gemini API.
Whether enrollment remains free after sign-in and region restrictions.
Instructor quality beyond names listed on the marketing page.
aiReview.tagline: Free 2-hour course on Gemini API and AI Studio
aiReview.description: Learn to build text, image, and code apps with Gemini API and Google AI Studio in a free intermediate Python course.
pros: Public catalog page describes a free intermediate course focused on Gemini API and Google AI Studio.
Listed skills include large language models, prompt engineering, Gemini API, and Google AI Studio.
Course page shows an update date of Jul 1, 2025 and a 2-hour, 6-lesson outline.
Google and Udacity publicly announced a free Gemini API course covering AI Studio.
cons: The candidate canonical URL is an enrollment path that redirects to a sign-in wall with no course content.
Lesson-level implementation quality and API version coverage cannot be verified without enrollment.
Requires intermediate Python, so it is not a zero-prerequisite reference.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Codelab that walks through Gemini in Google Cloud for log explanation and Cloud Function deployment troubleshooting. Useful as a hands-on tutorial, but it targets Gemini for Google Cloud/Code Assist in Console rather than the Gemini Developer API.
evidence: Canonical URL is Google Codelabs: troubleshooting-with-gemini.
Meta description: Gemini for Google Cloud to summarize logs, explain errors, and remediate issues.
Steps cover Cloud Functions Python sample, Log Explorer Explain this log entry, and Code Assist chat.
Cleanup uses gcloud functions delete; content licensed CC BY 4.0 / Apache 2.0.
uncertainty: Whether the Codelab UI and Gemini Log explanations still match current Cloud Functions/Gemini Console product names.
Whether unauthenticated function setup plus identity-token curl is still the recommended path.
aiReview.tagline: Hands-on lab for Gemini-assisted Cloud Function log troubles
aiReview.description: Learn to summarize logs, explain errors, and fix a failed Cloud Function deploy using Gemini in Google Cloud Console.
pros: Official Google Codelabs content with step-by-step Console, Logging, and Cloud Functions instructions.
Shows Gemini log explanations and chat prompts for diagnosing a MissingTargetException on deploy.
Includes setup, cleanup, curl verification, and links to Gemini Code Assist and Logging docs.
cons: Focuses on Gemini for Google Cloud observability, not the Gemini Developer API or SDKs.
Requires a billed Google Cloud project and enabling multiple APIs.
Lab text mixes function names (get_object_list vs get_order_list), which can confuse readers.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Codelab that walks through Gemini Code Assist in Cloud Shell IDE (chat, explain, generate, inline complete) on a Python Flask Cloud Run sample. Useful for Cloud IDE users, but it targets Code Assist/Cloud Assist rather than the Gemini Developer API.
evidence: Canonical URL is a Google Codelabs page titled A Tour of Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise for Developers in Google Cloud Shell Editor.
Meta description states use of Gemini Chat and inline assistance to generate and understand code.
Lab steps include enabling Cloud Assist in console, Cloud Shell IDE setup, Flask Cloud Run template, explain-this, Control+Enter generation, and optional GCS bucket IAM/public access.
uncertainty: Whether Code Assist UI and keyboard shortcuts still match the screenshots.
Whether the public gemini-codeassist-bucket still exists and is accessible.
Current pricing/entitlement for Standard vs Enterprise Code Assist.
aiReview.tagline: Hands-on Cloud Shell lab for AI-assisted coding
aiReview.description: Learn Cloud Shell IDE chat, inline completion, and code explanation on a Python Flask Cloud Run sample.
pros: Hosted on Google Codelabs with a clear step-by-step lab structure and stated prerequisites.
Covers chat, code explanation, comment-to-code generation, and inline suggestions in Cloud Shell IDE.
Uses a concrete Python Flask Cloud Run template plus optional GCS listing and cleanup steps.
cons: Does not teach the Gemini Developer API, SDKs, or AI Studio.
Requires a billed Google Cloud project with Code Assist enabled.
URL slug still references Duet AI; product naming in the path may be dated.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Codelab that walks through Gemini Code Assist in Cloud Shell Editor to generate tests and code for a Python app. Strong official tutorial quality, but it targets Code Assist in Google Cloud IDEs rather than the Gemini Developer API.
evidence: Canonical URL is a Google Codelabs page titled Introduction to testing with Gemini Code Assist.
Meta description: Use Gemini Code Assist to help you write tests for your code.
Lab clones github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/testing-with-duet-ai-codelab and uses Cloud Shell Editor plus Cloud AI Companion API enablement.
uncertainty: Whether the Codelab and Duet-era screenshots are fully current with 2026 Code Assist UI.
Exact Code Assist licensing/pricing for all Google Cloud account types.
Fit for a Gemini API-only directory versus Google Cloud AI coding tools.
aiReview.tagline: Official lab: generate tests and code in Cloud Shell
aiReview.description: Use Gemini Code Assist in Cloud Shell Editor to write tests, fix bugs, and extend a Python web app with step-by-step Google Cloud setup.
pros: Hosted on Google Codelabs with structured steps, screenshots, and sample prompts.
Covers chat and inline assistance for unittest generation, running tests, and iterative code fixes.
Uses a public GoogleCloudPlatform sample repo and Cloud Shell so the path is reproducible in-browser.
cons: Focuses on Gemini Code Assist / Cloud Code, not the Gemini Developer API or SDKs.
Requires a billed Cloud project with Gemini Code Assist enabled; some UI steps still mention Duet AI.
Model answers are acknowledged as non-deterministic, so lab snippets may not match live output.

No maintenance, versioning, or code-quality signals typical of directory tools.

HTTP fetch of the URL redirects to accounts.google.com sign-in
uncertainty: Exact app gallery contents, APIs, and docs behind login
Current availability of Gemini 3 Flash versus marketing copy
Precise pricing and quota terms for Apps vs API
aiReview.tagline: Official web workspace to prototype Gemini-powered apps
aiReview.description: Sign in to Google’s official studio to build and try Gemini-backed apps. Linked from developer docs; account required.
pros: Hosted on aistudio.google.com, Google’s official Gemini developer console.
Repeatedly cited from ai.google.dev as a build destination for Gemini models.
Directly relevant to Gemini API experimentation rather than third-party wrappers.
cons: Unauthenticated fetch only shows a Google Account login wall, not app docs or examples.

No public README or excerpt was provided to confirm feature list or pricing.

aiReview.summary: Official Chrome documentation hub for browser-managed on-device AI (Gemini Nano) and related web platform APIs. High-quality, maintained Google docs with API status, get-started guidance, and safety/UX notes; not a cloud Gemini API SDK.
evidence: Canonical URL https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/built-in titled Built-in AI | AI in Chrome.
Page states the browser provides and manages foundation and expert models for websites.
Linked from ai.google.dev curated readme as integrating Gemini Nano via Chrome built-in APIs.
Documents Prompt, Summarizer, Translator, Language Detector, Writer, Rewriter, and Proofreader APIs plus best-practice guides.
uncertainty: Current origin-trial and production availability of each API was not independently verified beyond the hub page.
Pricing of related cloud fallback (Firebase AI Logic) is not specified on this page.
aiReview.tagline: On-device web AI APIs managed by the browser
aiReview.description: Build web features with browser-managed models and task APIs for writing, translation, summarization, and prompting.
pros: Published on developer.chrome.com as official Built-in AI documentation.
Covers task APIs (Writer, Rewriter, Translator, Summarizer, Prompt, and others) and availability status.
Includes get-started requirements, origin-trial notes, polyfills, hybrid fallback, and debugging guidance.
Links ethics, model-download UX, and do/don't guidance for on-device AI.
cons: Targets Chrome built-in/on-device APIs rather than the cloud Gemini Developer API.
Several APIs depend on preview or origin-trial availability and browser support.

reference.excerpt:
# zero-plugins

Official Zero plugins — give your AI agent the ability to discover and pay for
new capabilities.

Zero is a search engine and payment layer for AI agents. With the Zero plugin
installed, your agent can find capabilities it doesn't have built in — image,
video, and audio generation, web scraping, real-time data, messaging, and
more — call them, and pay per use from a single wallet. No per-service
signups, no API keys to manage.

## Install Zero

The recommended way to install Zero is to let your agent install it and guide
you through setup. Just paste this to your agent:

```
Help me set up Zero — a tool that lets you find and use extra services you
don't have built in (image/video generation, search live social media, or
hosting a free webpage). It's free to set up.

Set it up by running the Zero CLI's setup (needs Node.js — install it first if
`npm` isn't available):

    npm i -g @zeroxyz/cli
    zero init
    zero auth login
```
